significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that the correct object is “linearly decodable … several layers before” output and that “onset layer, slope, and terminal stability” are predictively coupled to correctness, with “peak-then-decay” identifying retrieved-but-unexpressed facts; this is primarily a form-(iii) ordering and predictive-coupling claim, plus a limited mechanism in which late processing suppresses an available answer. It would predict a family of layerwise observations and sharpen interpretations of factual-recall stages studied by Geva et al. (2023, “Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models”) and output-oriented trajectories such as the Tuned Lens, although it would not by itself fully explain why decay occurs. The phenomenon and retrieval–output distinction are weighty and determinate, but the negative branch mainly rules out these trajectory features as a general discriminator and could leave early decodability, correctness prediction, and decay dissociated rather than selecting one alternative account. In the topic-substitution check, a generic statement that retrieval dynamics affect expressed knowledge would not merit 7; the score comes specifically from the asserted temporal ordering, predictive relation, and decay signature.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “per-example curve of retrieval strength across depth,” summarized by “onset layer, max, terminal value, area” and used as a correctness predictor and known-but-unsaid diagnostic. It is ex ante relative to answer emission because prompt residual states can flag likely failure before the answer is generated, giving an auditor or gating system a limited action window rather than merely explaining an observed error. A new model would require re-extracting the relation-conditioned probe, but the substantive conclusion predicts the same qualitative coupling between rise/stability/decay and correctness across factual-query tasks, rather than supplying only an unconstrained search procedure; it does not, however, specify transferable thresholds or numerical scaling. The topic alone supplies no such handle in the substitution check, so the reach score rests on this trajectory-based predictor, whose plausible users include factuality auditors beyond the immediate interpretability research line.
